notes: 13 of 13 searches used. (1) Several first-pass attributions rested on blended summaries; kept only what a returned excerpt stated. (2) MHRA: the June 2025 Safety Roundup was never returned; its reference was dropped. The returned MHRA statement (via GOV.UK/NI news and guidance summaries) says overweight patients taking Mounjaro should use a non-oral method in addition to the pill; the 'four weeks after starting and each dose increase' window is not in any retrieved MHRA text (a summary attributed it variously to MHRA, the SmPC and a GP notice) so it was removed; the Mounjaro SmPC (medicines.org.uk/emc/product/15481/smpc) was returned but only via summary, so a human should confirm the timing and decide whether to restore it with the SmPC cited. (3) NICE TA924: retrieved text is the original recommendation (triple therapy failed etc.) plus a NICE review consultation proposing an update aligned with NG28; the Aug 2026 updated wording was NOT retrieved, so the page uses only the generic 'some adults who meet set criteria, alongside diet and exercise'; recheck against the live TA924 page. (4) Dehydration: no NICE text found; replaced with a South West London ICB prescriber-sheet statement (retrieved via summary of the sheet). Gallstones: attributed to the NHS medicines page (two searches state it lists gallstones/gallbladder swelling) not the regional page; still blended-summary level evidence. (5) NHS pregnancy/alcohol/low sugar/anaphylaxis/weight programme claims were re-retrieved with differently worded queries and agree, but are still search summaries of nhs.uk/medicines/tirzepatide, not page text. 'Stopped if pregnancy occurs', driving/machinery advice, 'not used while breastfeeding', 'most common' and 'same day' urgency timing were removed as not retrieved. (6) Emergency routes: the retrieved NHS text gives no explicit 111/999 wording for this page; the one combined route sentence (published twice: serious-effects list and article) is textbook signposting by site rule, 2 textbook rows of 77 first-pass (2.6%); the six-month review wording keeps no percentage. (7) productType: kept 'small-molecule'. Vocabulary options: small-molecule = chemically synthesised medicine, majority of tablets, capsules and injections; recombinant-protein = human protein made by engineered cells (insulins, GH). Tirzepatide is a synthetic peptide, not a human protein from engineered cells (general knowledge, not retrieved, not published), and no 'peptide' id exists; 'other' (used by sibling semaglutide) is the alternative if the maintainer prefers. Kent and Medway newsletter calls it a 'new class' with a fatty-diacid moiety, consistent with a chemically modified peptide. (8) urlAlias 'mounjaro': not changed; brand name is retrieved (NHS, Cheshire and Merseyside, MHRA); check_batch reports any clash. Not checked against interactions.json: no tirzepatide entry there (count 0).
